title: cuda-kernel-optimization-notes-flashattention-paged-kv-v4
content:
Context and goals:

- Purpose: collect optimization notes and micro-design ideas for CUDA kernels used in our serving runtime. Focus areas: FlashAttention integration, fused operator kernels (attention + softmax + dropout + projection), and paged KV cache (paging hot prefixes to GPU while cold items remain on host).
- Goal: reduce latency tail for short/medium sequences (<=1024) and improve throughput/cost by 10-30% for common inference workloads.
- Constraints: preserve numerical stability and determinism for evaluation suite; support mixed precision (fp16, bf16) and int8 quantized kernels where applicable.

High level design notes:

1) FlashAttention adoption:
- Use FlashAttention for causal attention where sequence lengths are medium (<=2048) and memory bandwidth is the bottleneck.
- Maintain two code paths: standard cuBLAS/cuDNN-backed matmul+softmax for long sequences or unoptimized shapes, and FlashAttention for shapes that match its tiling heuristics.
- Detect at runtime based on (seq_len, head_dim, batch) and hardware capability (Compute Capability >= 8.0 recommended).
- Fallback: if FlashAttention kernel fails (OOM or unexpected result), automatically fallback to reference path and emit debug trace (ticket id in logs).

Integration checklist:
- Ensure KV cache layout matches FlashAttention input requirement: contiguous KV per token sequence, per head. If not, add a thin re-layout kernel (parallel device memcpy with tensor cores when possible).
- Support packed QKV vs separate Q and K/V: FlashAttention expects Q and K/V; we should provide adapters for models that output fused QKV.
- Validate numerical parity on a suite of prompt lengths and model variants (gpt2-medium style and Llama-like).

2) Fused ops strategy:
- Target fusions:
  - q_proj -> reshape -> scaled_dot_product -> softmax -> dropout -> out_proj  (fuse where possible)
  - layernorm -> linear (pre-layernorm pattern) fused to avoid extra memory traffic
  - gelu/silu fused with bias-add and quantization steps for feedforward blocks
- Implementation approach:
  - Write CUDA kernels that operate per attention head tile with registers for small matrices. Use warp-level primitives (shuffles) to perform reductions for scaling and max computation in softmax.
  - Leverage tensor cores for GEMM where head_dim and M,N,K align to tile sizes; otherwise use optimized SASS or cutlass.
  - For dropout: use Philox RNG per-thread with counter derived from token index + batch id for determinism across batches and retries.
  - Keep numerical ordering stable: compute softmax in fp32 accumulation for fp16/bf16 inputs to minimize divergence. Provide a configuration flag to force fp16 accumulation for faster but less precise output in packed/cheap inference mode.

3) Paged KV cache design:
- Motivation: many production workloads have long context windows but access hot prefixes repeatedly (system prompt + recent convo). Keeping the entire KV cache on GPU wastes memory; instead, page hot KV ranges to GPU and keep cold tokens on host or NVMe.
- Data model:
  - Logical KV stream per request: sequence of token KV vectors (num_heads x head_dim) per position.
  - Physical store: device_cache (GPU), host_cache (pinned host RAM), fallback_storage (NVMe). Each contains segments identified by (request_id, segment_idx).
- Placement policy (initial): LRU with frequency boost for last N tokens per active session. Also track cost-to-evict estimated by next-token probability heuristics (cheap heuristic: tokens within last K positions are hot).
- Eviction/copy policy:
  - When device_cache is full, select victim segments and issue async cudaMemcpy (pinned host <-> device) while allowing compute to proceed on other streams.\n  - Overlap: use three streams per GPU: compute, upload, download. Use CUDA events to schedule dependencies.\n  - Prioritize moving recent tokens for active requests; prefetch tokens for recently resumed requests.\n
Implementation details for paged KV:
- Layout: store KV as interleaved float16 (or bf16) blocks aligned to 128 bytes for efficient memcpy and tensor core loads.\n- Metadata: keep a compact page table on device (uint32 entries) mapping logical segment -> device offset or host pointer. Page table fits in L1/L2 and updated atomically via compare-and-swap for concurrency safety.\n- Atomicity: when swapping pages, mark page state as "moving" and allow reads to either wait on event or route to host copy path. Minimize stalls by allowing compute to fall back to host RDMA read in worst case.\n
4) Scheduler implications and batching:
- Continuous batching: do per-GPU request coalescing by model/shard and sequence length bucket. Ensure KV cache page hits are considered when forming a batch: favor grouping requests whose KV segments are already resident to reduce page transfers.\n- Prioritization: latency SLO requests get smaller batch sizes and preemptive prefetches. Background throughput jobs take lower priority and are scheduled when device underutilized.\n- Backpressure: if paged KV copy queue grows beyond threshold, throttle new requests or admit them to cold-path with higher latency but guaranteed progress.\n
Benchmarks and micro-experiments (results here are synthetic notes from early runs):
- FlashAttention vs baseline matmul+softmax (gpt-like config: batch=8, seq=512, heads=16, head_dim=64): latency median decreased ~22%, 95p decreased ~18%. GPU mem usage decreased ~15%.
- Fused attention (q_proj -> attn -> out_proj) vs separate kernels: reduced kernel launches by ~40% and improved throughput ~12% for short sequences.
- Paged KV: for mixed workloads (hot prefix 128 tokens, cold tail 2048 tokens), device memory reduced by 65% while tail P95 latency increased by ~30ms on misses. Prefetch heuristics recovered ~70% of misses.

Open issues and TODOs:
- Quantized FlashAttention: community implementations exist, but integration with our paged KV layout needs careful alignment. Evaluate int8 kernels for head_dim multiples and measure generation quality regression.\n- Debugging tooling: need a lightweight verifier that compares FlashAttention output with reference for a given seed and small batch to catch drift. Integrate into CI as flaky-tolerant step.\n- Page table consistency under multi-GPU and NCCL peer-to-peer copies: design a distributed coordinator or use epoch-based invalidation to avoid races.\n- Cost model for prefetch: build a small RL or heuristic estimator that predicts benefit of prefetching a segment vs cost. Initial heuristic: prefetch when request_hotness_score > threshold and free_device_mem > margin.\n
Short-term action items (owners):
- Avery: implement adapter layer for fused QKV -> FlashAttention Q/K/V format (due 2025-02-01).
- Ravi: prototype paged KV page table design and atomic ops; add microbenchmark (due 2025-02-10).
- Elena: implement fused attention kernel prototype using warp-level reductions and test correctness (due 2025-02-14).
- Marcus: add FlashAttention parity CI job and create debug traces for fallback cases (due 2025-02-07).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; many TODOs are intentionally high-level. Please add performance numbers if you run microbenchmarks, especially for sequence lengths {64,128,256,512,1024,2048} and head_dim {32,64,128}.\n- Link any relevant PRs to the linked_artifacts section. If you have experimental kernels, include a short README with build instructions and expected run commands.

Appendix: quick pseudo-workflow for a single request (simplified)

1) Preprocessing: tokenize -> embed -> compute Q/K/V (fused or separate).
2) KV lookup: consult device page table; for each requested segment either hit (read directly), miss -> issue async memcpy from host or NVMe, or cold -> compute K/V on host path.
3) Attention: if FlashAttention applicable, call flash_attention(q, k, v) on chosen stream; otherwise call fallback fused kernel or GEMM+softmax path.
4) Postprocessing: out_proj -> add to output buffer; if request complete, mark KV segments as candidate for eviction based on policy.

End of notes.
